root.name: Scotch Game: Relfsson Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bb5

overview: The Relfsson Gambit (MacLopez) plays 4.Bb5 instead of recapturing on d4, pinning the c6 knight while the d4 pawn stays with Black. Black can keep the pawn with ...Bc5 or ...Nf6 while White develops quickly with O-O and c3 for an Open Spanish-like attack. It is a rare surprise weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Castle quickly and play c3 to open lines against the centre
Use the pin on c6 and pressure e5 or f7
Regain the d4 pawn with Nxd4 when possible

black_ideas.idea: Keep the extra pawn with ...Bc5 or ...Nf6, ...d6
Return the pawn if needed for safe development

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with Black a pawn up after ...dxc3, or e-file open if White regains

character.notes: Open lines and a pawn offered; both sides must find concrete moves.

gambit.notes: Black can simply keep the d4 pawn if he wishes.

soundness.notes: Considered inferior to 4.Nxd4; Black can hold the extra pawn.

structure.notes: Centre opens at once, pieces rule.

approach.notes: A seldom-played sideline of the Scotch.

level.notes: Little to memorise but rewards open-game tactics.

character.reason: White is a pawn down for open lines and quick development.

gambit.reason: White leaves the d-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Inferior to the regular recapture; Black can hold the pawn.

structure.reason: Centre pawns come off and pieces take over.

level.reason: Dubious so not Beginner, little theory to learn.

plans.reason: White plays for fast development in return for the pawn.
